evidence: market-data.controller.ts getMarketDataBySymbol and updateMarketData both run `const [assetProfile] = await this.symbolProfileService.getSymbolProfiles([{ dataSource, symbol }])` followed by the same `if (!assetProfile && !isCurrency(getCurrencyFromSymbol(symbol))) throw new HttpException(getReasonPhrase(StatusCodes.NOT_FOUND), StatusCodes.NOT_FOUND)`

Both handlers repeat the ownership check `assetProfile?.userId === this.request.user.id && hasPermission(this.request.user.permissions, permissions.*OfOwnAssetProfile)` (canReadOwnAssetProfile vs canUpsertOwnAssetProfile)
When access is denied, getMarketDataBySymbol throws 404 or 403 based on `assetProfile.userId` (no optional chaining); updateMarketData always throws FORBIDDEN, so the copies disagree
getMarketDataOfMarkets uses `@HasPermission(permissions.readMarketDataOfMarkets)` + `HasPermissionGuard`, while the other handlers call `hasPermission(...)` inline
market-data.module.ts only declares MarketDataController and imports the providers it injects, which fits the module's single concern
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both files serve one concern: the market-data endpoints. market-data.module.ts only sets up MarketDataController and imports the providers its constructor injects. However, the controller repeats one access rule ("the asset profile must exist unless the symbol is a currency, and the caller needs the global permission or must own the profile and hold the own-profile permission") in two handlers: getMarketDataBySymbol and updateMarketData. The copies have already drifted. When access is denied, getMarketDataBySymbol returns 404 or 403 depending on assetProfile.userId and reads assetProfile.userId without optional chaining, which can throw when the currency fallback leaves assetProfile undefined. updateMarketData always returns 403. Permission checks also use two styles: getMarketDataOfMarkets uses the declarative @HasPermission/HasPermissionGuard, while the other two handlers call hasPermission(...) inline. The access rule should be in one shared helper or guard, so the unit fails the rubric's rule against duplicated invariants.

violations.message: The asset-profile existence and ownership/permission rule is copied in getMarketDataBySymbol and updateMarketData (getSymbolProfiles lookup, the isCurrency NOT_FOUND check, the canRead*/canUpsert* own-profile checks). The copies already differ: the denial status is 404/403 in one and always 403 in the other, and there is an unguarded `assetProfile.userId` dereference. Move this rule into one shared helper or guard.
